title: Not All Interpretation Methods Are Created Equal: Tiered Evaluation of AI Interpretability
abstract: arXiv:2611.31833v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As AI transitions to sociotechnical deployments, uninterpretable models pose serious threats to reliability, public trust and contestability. However, not all interpretation methods are created equal: for interpretability to enhance deployment safety and effectiveness, interpretation methods must be evaluated in a tiered system to differentiate evidence levels of trustworthiness, rather than validated through isolated interpretation instances. Our core vision is that elevating the evaluation of interpretation methods to a core AI assessment metric will drive robust knowledge discovery from data (KDD) and ensure safe, contestable sociotechnical deployments of AI. To this end, we propose TRUST, a tiered evaluation framework that builds upon the Predictability-Computability-Stability (PCS) principles for Veridical Data Science (VDS) and the Predictive, Descriptive and Relevant (PDR) foundations. translated_title: 并非所有解释方法都生而平等：AI可解释性的分层评估
translated_abstract: 随着AI转向社会技术部署，不可解释的模型对可靠性、公众信任和可争议性构成了严重威胁。然而，并非所有解释方法都生而平等：为了使可解释性能够提升部署的安全性和有效性，解释方法必须在一个分层体系中加以评估，以区分其可信度的证据等级，而不是通过孤立的解释实例进行验证。我们的核心愿景是，将解释方法的评估提升为核心AI评估指标，将推动稳健的知识发现（KDD），并确保AI在社会技术部署中的安全性和可争议性。为此，我们提出了TRUST，一个分层评估框架，它建立在真实数据科学（VDS）的可预测性-可计算性-稳定性（PCS）原则以及预测性、描述性与相关性（PDR）基础之上，以有效区分解释方法的可信度……
tldr: 提出了TRUST分层评估框架，将解释方法的评估提升为AI核心评估指标，以区分不同解释方法的可信度证据等级，从而推动稳健的知识发现并确保AI在社会技术部署中的安全性与可争议性。
en_tdlr: Proposes TRUST, a tiered evaluation framework that elevates interpretation method assessment to a core AI metric, differentiating evidence levels of trustworthiness to drive robust knowledge discovery and ensure safe, contestable sociotechnical deployments of AI.
